Name: reasoning_length_steering_vector
Title: Steering the Length of Thought: A Causal Vector for Reasoning Verbosity
Short Hypothesis: Reasoning trace length is controlled by a low-dimensional, causally manipulable subspace in activation space. A steering vector derived from long-versus-short trace contrasts can smoothly modulate verbosity at inference without retraining, preserving accuracy over a wide range.
Related Work: Turner et al. (2023) activation steering; Rimsky et al. (2024) CAA; Han et al. (2024) length control via prompting/RL. Prompt- and RL-based length control are coarse and require training. We show length is a manipulable activation direction, offering per-query, training-free, monotonic control and a mechanistic account of where length is represented.
Abstract: Controlling how long a model 'thinks' is central to efficient reasoning, yet current methods rely on prompting or reinforcement learning. We hypothesize that trace length is encoded in a compact activation subspace and can be steered causally. We construct a length-steering vector via difference-in-means between activations on naturally long versus short correct traces for matched problems, and refine it with a logistic length probe. Adding negative multiples of the vector shortens subsequent generation; positive multiples lengthen it. We characterize the accuracy-length response curve, seeking a regime where moderate shortening preserves accuracy (cutting overthinking) before a cliff where reasoning becomes truncated. We compare the steering knob against prompt instructions and token-budget forcing on the tokens/accuracy Pareto frontier, and test whether a single vector generalizes across tasks and layers. We probe whether the vector operates by modulating the verification-loop and commitment mechanisms studied elsewhere, connecting length control to specific reasoning sub-processes. The result is a training-free, interpretable dial for compute allocation and evidence that verbosity is a manipulable latent factor rather than an emergent, entangled property.
Experiments: 1. Mine matched problem pairs with long vs short correct traces (GSM8K, MATH). 2. Compute difference-in-means length vector at each layer; select layer by probe AUC. 3. Steer with coefficients in a sweep; record generated tokens and exact-match accuracy. 4. Plot accuracy vs mean tokens; identify the 'free lunch' shortening regime. 5. Baselines: 'answer concisely' prompt, hard token cap, budget-forcing ('Final answer:' injection). 6. Generalization: apply vector fit on MATH to GSM8K/BBH/code. 7. Mechanism link: measure change in verification-token frequency and commit-vector timing under steering.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Steering may degrade coherence or push activations off-distribution at large coefficients. A single linear vector may not capture length across regimes; optimal layer/coefficient may be problem-dependent. Length and correctness may be entangled such that no free-lunch regime exists for some tasks.
